extracted.intended_audience: exchange legal/operations staff, Equity Members and other market participants, SEC staff and securities market lawyers
extracted.subtask_description: A Federal Register notice of a self-regulatory organization's proposed rule change amending an exchange fee schedule (connectivity and port fees), including the exchange's statutory justifications, cost analyses, and discussion of Commission Staff review standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency with Section 6(b)(4) — equitable allocation of fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees must provide for the equitable allocation of reasonable dues, fees and other charges among Equity Members and other persons using any facility or system which the Exchange operates or controls (Section 6(b)(4) of the Act).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Exchange states the proposed fees are consistent with Section 6(b)(4) because they provide for an equitable allocation of reasonable dues and charges among users. Filings should explain how the fee allocation is equitable among different classes of users (e.g., Equity Members, non-Members, service bureaus, extranets).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency with Section 6(b)(5) — promote just and equitable principles, protect investors/public interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Fee changes should be designed to promote just and equitable principles of trade, remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system, and, in general, protect investors and the public interest (Section 6(b)(5)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The filing should explain how the proposed fees further the objectives of Section 6(b)(5), e.g., by promoting competition, enabling infrastructure investment, or otherwise protecting investors and the public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not unfairly discriminatory / not an undue burden on competition
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees must not be designed to permit unfair discrimination between customers, issuers, brokers and dealers, and must not create an undue burden on competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why the fee structure does not unfairly discriminate (e.g., identical treatment of similarly situated users or justification for differential treatment) and show that the fee will not produce an undue competitive burden. Provide comparisons across customer groups and demonstrate nondiscriminatory application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whether fee is constrained by significant competitive forces (Staff Guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: As an initial step, staff considers whether the fee is constrained by significant competitive forces — if so, that supports reasonableness without extensive cost proof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filings relying on a market-based / competition-based justification should explain the competitive dynamics (e.g., options for order-routing, alternatives for market participants) demonstrating that significant competition will constrain fees. Cite case law (NetCoalition) and relevant releases when making this argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-based justification as an alternative (Staff Guidance / BOX Order context)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an SRO cannot demonstrate that significant competitive forces constrain the fee, a cost-based discussion may be an alternative basis to show consistency with the Exchange Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using a cost-based approach, provide a detailed quantitative cost and revenue analysis to support the proposed fee. The Exchange cites BOX Order and Staff Guidance as requiring more comprehensive information when relying on cost recovery arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide specific quantitative information to support cost recovery claims
rubrics_metrics.description: If supporting a fee as cost-recovery, the filing should include specific information, including quantitative information, to support that argument (e.g., costs, allocations, projected revenues, profit margins).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Staff expects granular cost information (e.g., annual aggregate costs, allocation methodology, projected profit margins) and may require explanation of how costs were allocated and calculated. The filing here includes aggregate cost numbers and allocation descriptions to meet that expectation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop a record sufficient to enable Commission review (Remand Order standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission (per the Remand Order) directed exchanges to 'develop a record' and 'explain their conclusions, based on that record, in a written decision that is sufficient to enable [the Commission] to perform our review.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filings should assemble a comprehensive administrative record (supporting data, analyses, methodologies, and rationales) so Commission staff can meaningfully evaluate and, if necessary, not suspend or disapprove the filing. The Exchange documents its repeated, iterative filings and updated cost analyses in response to this standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain and document cost allocation across affiliated markets (no double-counting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost analyses must describe how costs are allocated among affiliated markets and ensure that no cost is allocated more than once; explain differences in allocation across affiliates when applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide narratives and numerical allocations showing how shared costs (e.g., gateways, matching engines, market data) were apportioned among MIAX entities, and why allocations may differ from affiliated filings (e.g., different number of matching engines or proprietary feeds). Address concerns about double-counting explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: High standards of transparency and disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Exchanges should meet high standards of transparency to demonstrate why each new fee or amendment meets the Act's requirements (reasonableness, equitable allocation, nondiscrimination).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include comprehensive documentation (cost analyses, revenue data, comparisons to other exchanges, methodological explanations). The Exchange emphasizes transparency is especially important when imposing access-related fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show fees will not result in excessive pricing or supra-competitive profit
rubrics_metrics.description: Filings should support that proposed fees are fair and reasonable and will not result in excessive pricing or supra-competitive profits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide projected revenues, projected profit margins, and explanation of assumptions; compare proposed margins with benchmarks or competitor margins where appropriate. The Exchange includes projected aggregated cost and profit figures to satisfy this concern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate exchange access fee parity / comparability to competing exchanges
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain how proposed fees relate to fees at competing (legacy) exchanges or why differences are justified; parity can be used to show reasonableness and promote competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide comparisons (price lists, revenue figures) from other exchanges (legacy vs non-legacy) and explain historical baselines. The Exchange argues parity with legacy exchanges promotes competition and investment ability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe service types, free allowances, and tiered pricing methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Fee filings should clearly describe the types of services being charged (e.g., 1Gb ULL, 10Gb ULL, FIX ports, MEO ports), what is provided (access to primary/secondary data centers), any free-port allowances, and the tiered price schedule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly state the number of free ports, the tiers and prices for additional ports, and whether fees apply to Members, non-Members, service bureaus, extranets, and how sessions/ports are counted. MIAX's filing specifies first 5 ports free, then $450 per port ≥6, and prior treatment of first 25 free.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe and justify network operations and support costs underlying connectivity fees
rubrics_metrics.description: When fees are for connectivity or access, filings should explain the nature of the costs being recovered (e.g., monitoring, nanosecond granularity performance analysis, continuous network improvements, multiple data centers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give concrete examples of operational activities and why they are necessary (e.g., monitoring with nanosecond granularity, maintaining primary/secondary/disaster recovery centers) and quantify their costs where possible. MIAX cites these operational reasons in support of higher connectivity fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain competitive impact of fee approval/denial on exchange's ability to invest and compete
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing should analyze how the fee will affect the exchange's financial ability to invest in infrastructure, marketing, product development, and to competitively price transaction fees (including possible subsidization effects).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe how revenue from non-transaction fees can be used to subsidize transaction fees or invest in products, and explain harms from denial (e.g., inability to achieve fee parity, adverse competitive effects). The Exchange argues denial would disadvantage non-legacy exchanges relative to legacy exchanges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide historical context and comparisons to prior regulatory treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Filings should situate the proposed fee in regulatory and market history (e.g., prior filings, Staff Guidance issuance, BOX Order, D.C. Circuit decisions) to explain why current standards are being applied and how prior baselines affect the proposed fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite relevant Commission, court decisions, prior exchange filings, and explain how historical fee baselines (established pre-2019 by legacy exchanges) influence competitive dynamics and the reasonableness assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyze subscriber behavior and revenue sensitivity (retention/projection scenarios)
rubrics_metrics.description: Support for fee changes may include analyses of how subscribers will react (e.g., potential port terminations) and revenue sensitivity under different subscriber retention scenarios.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The filing may include projected revenue if all subscribers remain versus scenarios with some attrition; MIAX references IEX's analysis as an example, and explains why it did or did not perform a similar projection for this amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural compliance with filing rules and availability of proposed rule text
rubrics_metrics.description: Filings must state the statutory and rule provisions under which they are submitted (e.g., Section 19(b)(1), Rule 19b-4) and make the text of the proposed rule change available at specified locations (exchange website, principal office, Commission's Public Reference Room).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include required citations, file/docket numbers, and provide links/locations where the full text and supporting documents can be examined (MIAX provided website link and physical availability). For immediate effectiveness, identify the appropriate rule provision (e.g., 19b-4(f)(2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite and address precedent (BOX Order, Staff Guidance, D.C. Circuit cases) and how filing complies
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing should acknowledge relevant precedent and administrative guidance (e.g., BOX Order disapproving connectivity fee, Staff Guidance on fee filings, Susquehanna, SIFMA/NASDAQ litigation) and explain how the present filing complies with or is distinguished from those precedents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly discuss prior Commission and court decisions that shaped the 'Revised Review Process' and explain how the filing satisfies the standards articulated therein (e.g., additional cost detail, allocation methods).
